purpose: Functional B200 integration validation, not a strategy efficacy experiment

agent.configuration_note: One optimization round explicitly requested; host NCU permission denial disclosed. Dedicated-container sandbox override recorded in original manifest. Credentials stayed on local Mac through SSH tunnel.

plan.question: Does prefetching the dense persistent kernel's Q/K/V tensor-map descriptors during CTA setup reduce dispatch-inclusive attention latency without changing numerical results?
plan.change: In candidate.cu, modify only fwd_kernel_fa4: immediately after the tid/warp declaration and before register redistribution/tmem allocation, add a compile-time !PAGED guard and tid==0 block issuing three inline PTX prefetch.tensormap instructions for &mapQ, &mapK, and &mapV (64-bit pointer operands). This gives descriptor fetching the existing setup work to overlap. Keep tensor maps, data movement, arithmetic, barriers, scheduling, dispatch, API, and all other kernels unchanged. Do not implement during the plan invocation.
plan.expected_result: Unverified prediction: a small reduction, possibly below measurement noise, in unprofiled dispatch-inclusive CUDA-event latency versus the seed candidate; no numerical change is expected because descriptor prefetch is a cache hint. Controller timing and correctness determine acceptance; no gain is claimed in advance. Seed median candidate latencies are 0.081727996468544 ms causal, 0.10145599767565727 ms noncausal, and 0.07740800082683563 ms GQA; seed score is 1.4528381280020026. Assess all three cases under the unchanged controller workloads, repeats, correctness seeds, and acceptance criteria.

observations: The seed is valid and all three configured cases are correct and supported.
launch_ws routes eligible dense hd128 inputs to fwd_kernel_fa4, which takes grid-constant Q/K/V tensor maps and performs tmem/barrier setup before TMA work.
No explicit prefetch.tensormap instruction appears in the candidate.
evidence.limitations: Seed timings do not isolate descriptor latency. Existing historical source comments are not new profiling evidence. Prefetch may be neutral or regress because descriptors may already be cached and additional instructions cost time.

plan.validation: In the implementation invocation make this single source edit, then leave numerical correctness and unprofiled timing to the independent controller using task.json. Do not run NCU: task constraints report ERR_NVGPUCTRPERM and prohibit retrying. No GPU commands or diagnostics are needed for this plan.

outcome.observation: Executed the registered plan without changing plan.json. Added three inline PTX prefetch.tensormap instructions for mapQ, mapK, and mapV, using 64-bit pointer operands inside !PAGED and tid==0 guards immediately after the tid/warp declaration in fwd_kernel_fa4. Source diff verification passed. No GPU commands were run; compilation, numerical correctness, and timing remain unmeasured pending the independent controller.
outcome.interpretation: The edit implements the proposed descriptor-prefetch cache hint while leaving the remaining source unchanged. Existing seed measurements establish baseline validity and latency only; they do not establish descriptor latency as a bottleneck or demonstrate a benefit from this edit. The predicted small latency reduction remains unverified and may be neutral or negative.
outcome.next_action: Have the independent controller compile and evaluate the modified candidate on all three unchanged task cases with configured correctness seeds and timing repeats, then apply its keep/reject criteria.

diagnostic_trial.original_failure: Evidence validator rejected an empty stderr file alongside substantive valid evidence. Generated profile.py also shadowed the standard library during reference import.

limitations: No repeated multi-arm GPU efficacy experiment
